input.explanation:
The incident was read as a pure upstream failure (api.io-pay.example returning 503 for card lookups), but the code in this service cannot survive that input: the account page blows up on its own path regardless of what the provider returns.

Two faults in this repository, both on the account page path:

1. `Account.__init__` accepts `total_cents` and `total_this_month_cents` but only assigns `self.purchases`. Any read of `account.total_this_month_cents` (which `average_spend_per_item_this_month` does on every account page render) raises `AttributeError`. The account page therefore fails for every shopper, which matches the observed 100% error rate that a restart did not clear and that no deploy in the preceding week caused - the defect was latent until this code path was exercised.

2. `average_spend_per_item_this_month` divides by `len(bought)` with no guard. For a shopper with no purchases in the current month - the common case early in a billing month, and the case for the shopper in the error line - this raises `ZeroDivisionError` and takes the whole page down rather than degrading to a sensible "no spend yet" value.

The fix stores all three constructor arguments on the instance and returns 0 when there are no purchases in the current month, so the average is well defined for every shopper. Tests cover the shopper who bought, the shopper who bought nothing this month (previously a crash), the shopper with no purchases at all, and that the totals passed to the constructor are actually readable.

Upstream 503s still need their own handling in the caller, but this service should not be the thing that breaks: with these changes the account page renders its spend summary for every shopper instead of erroring.
input.summary: Make account spend summary safe: store all Account totals and return 0 average when no purchases this month
